legacy_root.title: Extract dynamic fan-out and barrier semantics under partial failure
legacy_root.question_or_target: How do existing engines express map-over-unknown-N with a barrier, and specifically what happens at the barrier when K of N children fail — the exact case where this estate measured a fan-in deadlock from one hung agent?
legacy_root.canonical_mechanism: Map-N is Map/expand/withItems/chord-header/WhenAll/concurrent activities. Barriers are map-run completion, trigger_rule, failFast, chord body, or Task.WhenAll. Default K-of-N is almost always K=N except AWS Distributed Map, which exposes an explicit tolerated-failure budget defaulting to zero. The local no-timeout pathology is named on Celery: task_time_limit defaults to 'No time limit', so a hung chord header never unlocks.

named_engine_record.why_this_matches_local_pathology: Estate finding: parallel() has no per-agent timeout, so one hung agent deadlocks the phase. Celery documents Default: No time limit on task_time_limit and a chord body that waits for every header result — a hung header task is the same fan-in deadlock.

claims.canonical_mechanism: Map-over-unknown-N is the Map state (Distributed mode). The barrier is Map Run completion. K-of-N is ToleratedFailureCount / ToleratedFailurePercentage; both default to zero, so any child failure fails the map.
claims.quoted_barrier_policy: Its default value is zero, which means the Map State will fail if any
claims.k_of_n_on_child_failure: Default K=N (zero tolerated failures). Raising ToleratedFailureCount allows N-K failures before the map fails with States.ExceedToleratedFailureThreshold.
claims.per_child_timeout: Child executions may set TimeoutSeconds; timed-out items count toward the tolerated-failure budget.
claims.strongest_caveat: Inline Map historically lacked the same tolerated-failure fields; quotes here are Distributed Map plus the ASL spec.

claims.canonical_mechanism: Map-over-unknown-N is a chord header group. The barrier is the chord body, which runs only after every header task has returned. Any header exception fails the callback with ChordError; remaining header tasks still run.
claims.quoted_barrier_policy: The chord callback result will transition to the failure state, and the error is set
claims.k_of_n_on_child_failure: Default is all-or-fail for the callback (K=N successes). Header members are not cancelled on first failure; the body still goes to FAILURE/ChordError.
claims.per_child_timeout: task_time_limit Default: No time limit. A hung header task never unlocks the chord — the local no-timeout fan-in deadlock.
claims.strongest_caveat: A result backend is required for chords; without it the unlock path is a different failure mode than a hung child.

claims.canonical_mechanism: Map-over-unknown-N is mapped task expansion (expand()). The barrier is the downstream task's trigger_rule over mapped indexes. Default all_success requires every upstream mapped index to succeed before the reduce/join runs.
claims.k_of_n_on_child_failure: Default all_success: any mapped-index failure blocks the join. all_done waits for terminal states including failures; one_failed fires on the first failure without waiting.
claims.per_child_timeout: default_task_execution_timeout empty/None: operators are never timed out by default — a hung mapped index holds the DAG run.
claims.strongest_caveat: Cluster policy or DAG default_args can install a timeout; the shipped config default remains empty.

claims.canonical_mechanism: Map-over-unknown-N is withItems/withParam template expansion. The barrier is template/DAG completion. Template failFast fails the template when any child pod has failed. DAG failFast defaults true: stop scheduling new nodes on first failure, then wait for in-flight nodes before failing the DAG.
claims.quoted_barrier_policy: FailFast, if specified, will fail this template if any of its child pods has failed
claims.k_of_n_on_child_failure: Default DAG failFast=true is fail-fast, not K-of-N. failFast=false runs every branch to completion. There is no native 'succeed if K of N children succeed' counter analogous to Step Functions.
claims.per_child_timeout: activeDeadlineSeconds is optional; unset means no template-level deadline.
claims.strongest_caveat: Optional per-pod deadlines exist but are not required; Celery's documented 'No time limit' is the named local-pathology match.

claims.canonical_mechanism: Map-over-unknown-N is N concurrent activity invocations joined by the workflow. Contrast with the local pathology: an Activity Execution MUST set Start-To-Close or Schedule-To-Close. Default Schedule-To-Close is infinity, but the docs still require one of the two fields.
claims.quoted_barrier_policy: An Activity Execution must have either this timeout (Start-To-Close) or the
claims.k_of_n_on_child_failure: Join semantics live in workflow code (all vs allSettled). A failed activity raises into the workflow; the platform does not define a K-of-N map barrier.
claims.per_child_timeout: Required Start-To-Close or Schedule-To-Close — Temporal is the contrast engine, not the no-timeout pathology.
claims.strongest_caveat: An author can still set a huge Schedule-To-Close; the documented requirement to set a timeout field is the contrast.

source_lineage.quote: An Activity Execution must have either this timeout (Start-To-Close) or the
The default Schedule-To-Close Timeout is ∞ (infinity).
start_to_close_timeout: timedelta | None

claims.canonical_mechanism: Map-over-unknown-N is firing one activity per item without await, then Task.WhenAll as the barrier. WhenAll completes only after every work item completes; a faulted child faults WhenAll.
claims.quoted_barrier_policy: When the orchestrator passes the task array to `Task.WhenAll`, it returns a task that doesn't complete until all copy operations complete.
claims.k_of_n_on_child_failure: Task.WhenAll is all-success: one failed activity fails the join. There is no built-in tolerated-failure percentage.
claims.per_child_timeout: No required per-activity timeout in the fan-out sample; orchestration/activity timeouts are optional host settings.
claims.strongest_caveat: The quoted page is the official fan-out sample, not a spec clause forbidding WhenAny.
